stem.en: How do seeds and fruits affect where plants can survive?

text.en: Seeds let a plant live with no water at any stage of its life.

feedback.en: Seed plants still need water to live. Gymnosperms do not need it for fertilisation.

text.en: Fruits let a plant make its food without any sunlight.

feedback.en: Food is made by photosynthesis in the leaves. A fruit helps to spread seeds.

text.en: Seeds and fruits keep each young plant beside its parent.

feedback.en: This is the opposite of what happens: fruits help spread seeds to new locations.

text.en: Seeds hold food, and fruits help spread them to new places.

feedback.en: Yes. This helps flowering plants live in a wide range of environments.

explanation.en: A seed protects the embryo and holds stored food. A fruit helps carry seeds to new locations. Together these let angiosperms occupy a wide range of environments.

hints.en: Think about what a seed carries and what a fruit does.
